title: Beyond Fixed Benchmarks and Worst-Case Attacks: Dynamic Boundary Evaluation for Language Models
claim: A fixed calibrated difficulty scale can be extended on demand with new boundary items when a new model exceeds its coverage.
layout: 1 panel, horizontal number line, left-to-right, red extension beyond the panel range
description: A single wide panel on a light gray background centers on a horizontal axis labeled β̂ (logits), with arrows at both ends. The left part of the axis is dashed gray. The middle is solid gray with tick marks. The right part is dashed red. Small black dots above the axis form the DBE anchor set, calibrated from the M=9 panel. Nine blue circles below the axis mark the reference panel of open-weight LLMs, and a few are labeled Mistral Nemo-12B, Gemma 3-12B, Gemma 3-27B and Qwen2.5 72B-AWQ. At the far right, red dots mark SGBS-generated items. A dashed red arrow is labeled 'scale extends on demand'. A red star below the axis marks the new model, with θ̂_new outside the panel's range. Red highlights draw the eye to the extension on the right.
caption: Dynamic Boundary Evaluation (DBE) builds a calibrated difficulty scale and extends it on demand. The anchor set (black dots) is calibrated on a category-specific Rasch logit scale $\hat\beta$ using responses from a fixed $M=9$ reference panel (blue circles). A new model is first evaluated against the existing anchors. If its estimated ability $\hat\theta_{\mathrm{new}}$ lies within the panel-covered range, the anchor set suffices. If it lies outside this range, Skill-Guided Boundary Search (SGBS) generates new boundary items near the target model's $p\approx 0.5$ region (red dots), which are then calibrated onto the same scale through panel responses. DBE therefore extends the ruler when needed rather than rebuilding it from scratch.
abstract: Evaluating large language models (LLMs) today rests on fixed benchmarks that apply the same set of items to any model, producing ceiling and floor effects that mask capability gaps. We argue that the most informative evaluation signal lies at the boundary, where the per-prompt pass probability is near $0.5$ under random-sampling decoding strategy, and propose Dynamic Boundary Evaluation (DBE), which actively locates each model's boundary and places it on a globally comparable difficulty scale. DBE delivers three artifacts: (i) a calibrated item bank covering safety, capability, and truthfulness, with per-item difficulty labels validated across $9$ reference LLMs; (ii) Skill-Guided Boundary Search (SGBS), a search algorithm that finds boundary items for a given target LLM using only API-level query access; and (iii) an evaluation protocol that places a new LLM on a unified ability scale and grows the evaluation set adaptively when the target falls outside the bank's coverage. We instantiate DBE on four categories spanning safety (harmful request refusal, over-refusal), capability (constrained instruction following), and truthfulness (multi-turn sycophancy resistance). The resulting evaluation covers a broader model spectrum without saturation while remaining compatible with existing datasets.
